why:
The quote is real but the finding's two consequences are both false, and the field's whole purpose is unavailable in this fork by recorded decision.

**1. Quote — exists, but truncated in a way that reverses the claimed behaviour.** `hooks.md:631` carries the sentence verbatim. It is, however, the first of four sentences in that table row. The row continues: "Absent until the first user input. {/* min-version: 2.1.196 */}Requires Claude Code v2.1.196 or later". So the CLAIMED BEHAVIOUR — "`prompt_id` is a common input field on **every** hook event" — is contradicted by the very row quoted: it is absent on every event before first user input, and gated on a Claude Code version.

**2. Our state — literally true.** `SdkAutomationInput` does start at `/Users/i.i.gavrikov/Desktop/work/nessy-desktop/packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:742` and carries no `prompt_id`. Re-running the grep with the globs quoted (the submitted command dies on zsh with "no matches found") and with `-a`: 0 hits in `packages`/`apps` `.ts`/`.tsx`. The only repo hits are the sweep's own JSON and one plan.

**3a. One layer down — `SdkAutomationInput` does not gate delivery, so "no field" ≠ "hooks can't see it".** Both emitters that actually reach a hook are unfiltered pass-throughs, not allowlists:
- `packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:640-646` — `hookCommandStdinPayload` returns `JSON.stringify({ ...input, hook_event_name: ..., ...(cwd) })`
- `packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:53` — `NESSY_EVENT_DATA: sanitizeForShell(JSON.stringify(input))`
- `packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-automation.ts:1643` — `const enrichedInput: SdkAutomationInput = { ...input, ... }`, spreading the Claude SDK's own hook-callback object

A `prompt_id` present on the incoming SDK input lands on the hook's stdin verbatim with zero code change. The TS interface is a documentation surface here, not a filter. (`sdk-bridge.ts` is an allowlist, but only for the `NESSY_*` convenience vars, and upstream has no `$CLAUDE_PROMPT_ID` either.)

**3b. One layer up — the producer is the vendored SDK, and at our pin it does not emit the field.** `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk@0.3.183` (pinned in root, `packages/core`, `packages/shared`) declares `BaseHookInput` at `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts:156-165` as `session_id`, `transcript_path`, `cwd`, `permission_mode?`, `agent_id?`, `agent_type?`, `effort?` — no `prompt_id`, matching the row's v2.1.196 gate. There is nothing upstream to pass through. "Implementing" this means fabricating a UUID our own runtime invents.

**3c. The stated purpose is structurally absent, and recorded as a deliberate product difference.** `prompt_id`'s documented value is correlating hook output with the OTel `prompt.id` attribute; `monitoring-usage.md:459,598` puts `prompt.id` exclusively on **events**, "never attached to metrics… intentionally excluded from metrics". This fork emits no OTel events at all. `packages/shared/src/telemetry/usage-metrics.ts:28-49` records that as a decision, not an omission: data points carry exactly `backend`, `model`, `type`, `cost_reporting`; of the standard attribute table "This fork exports NEITHER" (`session.id`, `user.id`); "This fork implements none of those flags" (`OTEL_LOG_*`); "For a bank fork the narrower set is the point… Any widening… is a privacy decision to be made on purpose, not an omission to be patched." Every `OTEL_*` occurrence elsewhere in the repo is managed-settings env passthrough (`config/managed-env.ts:164-168`, `config/managed-approval.ts:78-84`), not an emitter. A synthesized `prompt_id` would correlate with nothing that exists.

Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` §3 (checked: seatbelt wildcard, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries) — but the telemetry deviation it depends on is an equivalent in-code recorded decision.
correctedState:
`SdkAutomationInput` (`packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:742`) declares no `prompt_id`, and nothing in `packages`/`apps` sets one — but that is a typing/documentation gap, not a delivery gap, and it has no behavioural consequence today.

Delivery: the payload a command hook reads is built by pass-through spread — `hookCommandStdinPayload` (`packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:640`) is `JSON.stringify({ ...input, … })`, `NESSY_EVENT_DATA` (`:53`) is `JSON.stringify(input)`, and `hooks-automation.ts:1643` spreads the SDK's own callback object. Any `prompt_id` on the incoming input already reaches a hook verbatim.

Producer: the field is emitted by Claude Code v2.1.196+; the vendored `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk@0.3.183` `BaseHookInput` (`sdk.d.ts:156-165`) does not declare it, so at our pin there is nothing to pass through. It will start flowing on its own at the SDK bump, without a code change; the only work a bump warrants is adding the optional field to `SdkAutomationInput` so matchers can name it.

Purpose: `prompt.id` is an OTel **event** attribute (`monitoring-usage.md:459,598`), and this fork deliberately exports only two metric counters with `backend/model/type/cost_reporting` and no event channel or correlation identifiers at all — recorded at `packages/shared/src/telemetry/usage-metrics.ts:28-49` as a bank-fork privacy decision. There is no `prompt.id` in this product to correlate a `prompt_id` with.
